mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below the median market return at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which erode consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, indicates supply-side stress that raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the federal funds rate below 2% combined with a concurrent surge in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 4% monthly YoY indicates a shift from restrictive to accommodative policy amid high inflation, which historically precedes equity market volatility and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as markets anticipate policy easing.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops below 2% AND CPIAUCSL YoY > 4% in the same month
regime_hint: transition from high inflation to easing cycle
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (p > 0.05), or the event occurs fewer than 3 times in a 10-year sample.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 300,000 coincident with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals an overheating labor market, which raises wage inflation and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in triggered episodes (p > 0.10), or the mechanism fails to trigger in at least 2 out of the last 5 late-cycle periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (p > 0.05), or the mechanism fails to trigger at least once per year on average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly contraction in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) of more than 1% indicates broad-based supply chain stress, which raises costs and reduces output, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative in triggered episodes (p > 0.10), or fewer than 3 such co-contractions occur in a 10-year span.
